lessons.title: Germplasm and the planting plan
lessons.html:
Germplasm and the planting plan

Germplasm is the living genetic material that breeders work with: seed of breeding lines, inbred lines, parent lines, landraces, populations and new crosses. In a breeding programme, every season starts with preparing germplasm according to the breeder's plan, so that the right seed is planted in the right plot. If seed packets are mixed up, a whole season of breeding work can be lost.

The breeder's plan

Before planting, the breeder prepares a planting list or nursery book. It lists:

  • Each entry or pedigree to be planted, with its unique code
  • The source of the seed: inventory location, packet or envelope number
  • The number of seeds or rows per entry
  • The field, block, range and row where it will be planted
  • Any special treatment, such as seed treatment or planting date

Your job is to turn this list into ready-to-plant packets that match the plan exactly.

The germplasm store

Germplasm is stored in a cold, dry store or seed bank to keep it alive for many years. Each seed lot has a location code (shelf, box, position) in the inventory system. Seed is valuable and often irreplaceable. A landrace collected from a village decades ago may not exist anywhere else.

Preparing to work

  • Get the final planting list printed or loaded on a tablet with barcode scanning.
  • Prepare packets or envelopes, labels, a balance or seed counter and clean trays.
  • Allow seed taken from cold storage to warm up in sealed containers before opening, so that moisture does not condense on it.
  • Work at a clean bench, one entry at a time.

Wear gloves if seed is treated and follow the treatment label for handling.

lessons.title: Preparing, checking and recording packets
lessons.html:
Preparing, checking and recording packets

Counting or weighing seed

  1. Find the source lot using the location code and confirm its label matches the planting list.
  2. Count the number of seeds required, by hand, counting board or electronic counter. For larger lists, seed may be weighed using the seed mass per 100 seeds.
  3. Put the seed in the packet and seal it.
  4. Label the packet with the plot or row number, entry code and any other information required. Barcode labels reduce writing errors.
  5. Return the source lot to its exact location and update the inventory quantity.

Checking

  • Check every packet against the list: plot number, entry code and quantity.
  • Use a second person or barcode scan for verification.
  • Sort packets in planting order: by field, range and row, so that planters can work quickly without mistakes.
  • Pack sorted packets into labelled boxes or planting trays per field.

Problems to report

ProblemAction
Not enough seed in the source lotReport to the breeder before using it all; seed may need to be kept as a reserve
Seed looks mouldy or damagedReport; a germination check may be needed
Label on source lot does not match the listStop and check with the breeder; never guess
Missing source lotSearch the inventory history and report

Records

The inventory must show how much seed was taken from each lot, on what date, by whom and for which nursery or trial. Breeders rely on these records to trace every plant back to its origin. Save and back up the electronic files.

Key points

  • Germplasm is valuable and often irreplaceable genetic material.
  • Packets must match the breeder's planting list exactly.
  • Warm cold-stored seed in sealed containers before opening.
  • Check every packet, sort in planting order and update the inventory.
  • Report low stock, damaged seed and label mismatches; never guess.
